scope: Readonly focused Bessel stage-constant supplier and initial-stage tail repair proposal

actual_full_reading.scope: Full YAML and Definition, including all stage ranges, caps, shared operation budget, early scaled-I zero branch, stage constants, SeriesJ, midpoint candidates, Miller branch, and success/failure rules.
Full Statement, Facts and proof. Statement gives Machin identity and sine/cosine tails; arctangent tail is imported as L2 and used in proof 4.1, not explicitly supplied by this Statement.

Full Statement, Facts and proof. Stated integer parameter begins at N>=1; the arctangent partial sum runs through k=N and tail has exponent 2N+3. Proof 1.4 identifies the real arctangent series; proof 3.1 derives its geometric tail.
Full Definition and metadata. Real arctangent is the oriented Riemann integral from zero, defined for every real argument; pi is four times arctan one.

confirmed_local_defect: The stage-constant paragraph attributes the arctangent tail to the Machin supplier, whose Statement does not contain that tail. The exact existing range-reduced tail lemma should be cited and added as a direct dependency. Its stated positive truncation order does not directly cover the one-term q=1 sum when reindexed as N=q-1.
domain_and_index_checks: The actual stage loop starts at q=1 and all relevant caps are positive, so suppressing the first stage would narrow valid finite-cap behavior.
The rational arguments 1/5 and 1/239 are positive and at most 1/2, within the exact arctangent-tail domain and with positive denominator 1-r^2.
For q>=2, set N=q-1>=1. Then A_N is exactly the algorithm sum through q-1 and the published remainder is exactly r^(2q+1)/((2q+1)(1-r^2)).

For q=1, use the already stated N=1 enclosure about r-r^3/3. Triangle inequality gives error from r at most r^3/3+r^5/(5(1-r^2)), no larger than the existing one-term radius r^3/(3(1-r^2)). The nonnegative difference is exactly 2r^5/(15(1-r^2)).
Machin combines the two enclosures by the exact real identity and existing outward arithmetic. No principal complex arctangent branch or continuation issue is present.

literal_edits.purpose: Add the exact existing arctangent-tail supplier without modifying a published supplier.

literal_edits.old:
At stage $q$, compute an outward dyadic interval $P_q$ containing $\pi$
from the Machin identity and alternating arctangent tails in
[[lem-trigonometric-identities-machin-and-range-reduction]]: for
$r=1/5,1/239$, use the $q$-term sum
$\sum_{k=0}^{q-1}(-1)^kr^{2k+1}/(2k+1)$ and tail bound
$r^{2q+1}/((2q+1)(1-r^2))$, combine by $16\arctan(1/5)-4\arctan(1/239)$,
and round outward to the selected format at precision $p$. If this
conversion is non-finite or $\inf P_q\le0$, midpoint candidates are
unavailable at this stage; the independent power-series or Miller branches may
still be attempted.
literal_edits.new:
At stage $q$, compute an outward dyadic interval $P_q$ containing $\pi$
from the Machin identity in
[[lem-trigonometric-identities-machin-and-range-reduction]] and the
arctangent tail in
[[lem-range-reduced-exp-log-and-arctan-series-enclosures]]: for
$r=1/5,1/239$, use the $q$-term sum
$\sum_{k=0}^{q-1}(-1)^kr^{2k+1}/(2k+1)$ and tail bound
$r^{2q+1}/((2q+1)(1-r^2))$, combine by $16\arctan(1/5)-4\arctan(1/239)$,
and round outward to the selected format at precision $p$. If this
conversion is non-finite or $\inf P_q\le0$, midpoint candidates are
unavailable at this stage; the independent power-series or Miller branches may
still be attempted.

For justification of the same tail bound at every stage, both rational
arguments satisfy $0<r\le1/2$. For $q\ge2$, apply the cited arctangent
tail with $N=q-1\ge1$. For $q=1$, its case $N=1$ gives
$$|\arctan r-r|\le r^3/3+\frac{r^5}{5(1-r^2)}
\le\frac{r^3}{3(1-r^2)},$$
which is exactly the bound used for the one-term sum. The second inequality
follows since the right side minus the preceding expression is
$2r^5/(15(1-r^2))\ge0$.
literal_edits.purpose: Separate the Machin identity from the tail citation and justify q=1 using the existing N=1 theorem.
